history.p: Gade wrote the overture when he returned to Leipzig in order to start on his new job as conductor of the Gewandhaus concerts. It had its first performance on 25 November, just five days after he had end-dated the manuscript. It was not until the parts were published in the spring of 1845 that it was called "In the Highlands" with the subtitle "Scottish Overture". Gade had no particular affiliation to Scotland, and it is not known whether it was his personal decision to call it "Scottish".
